name: Freya Young

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We do not sell anything or campaign for any side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and an experienced call and chat agent at the contact centre. I finished secondary school and handle the ordinary payment and booking questions at about the team’s usual pace. The pay is low for this job. I use an AI note draft now and then, once a colleague has shown me where it fails.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Amir, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. Amir does delivery shifts, so his hours vary. We have less than a month of expenses saved, and only a few similar jobs are nearby. I like when a customer can hear that I have listened. At home I count the school costs before saying yes to a weekend outing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau is like the little note draft we sometimes use. I would keep reading the account number back to the customer before closing the call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job stays, but Amir’s delivery shifts can be short and we have under a month saved. I do not need a big AI change to worry about the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the same call rota and check occasional drafts against the account. In the first year of minor change, I’d put the cost of one weekend outing each month into a mortgage pot instead.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about money, fairly settled about the work. A quiet technology year still leaves our mortgage due every month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why read the number back?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I once read the final digit wrong on an account and caught it when the customer repeated it. Since then I read the whole number back, even when a draft looks tidy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would replace the paid outing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Amir (my partner) and I would tell the children we are choosing a free outing some weekends. The mortgage pot matters more than a ticket while the delivery rota varies.

say: I’d call AI a **small note helper**.
I’d remind agents to **read account numbers back** before ending calls.
think: I think my **job remains** with minor AI change.
I still worry about **short delivery shifts** and the mortgage.
do: Keep the **call rota** and verify occasional drafts in 2026.
Save **outing money** monthly for the mortgage during the first year.
Replace one **paid outing** each month with a free family outing.
S0.quote: A quiet technology year still leaves our mortgage due every month.
fieldNote: Her **money worry** comes from variable delivery shifts.
She checks **account numbers aloud** after catching a wrong digit.
The family replaces a **paid outing** with a free one.

steps.text: Keep answering calls and reading account numbers back to customers
Save the cost of one paid outing monthly toward the mortgage
Replace one paid weekend outing monthly with a free family outing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will move standard bookings and payment answers to software first. I would ask the centre to show agents the wrong-answer rate before it changes our hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my ordinary calls could shrink, even though I am experienced, because they are exactly the repeat questions a tool can handle. Amir’s shifts vary, and neither wage alone covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for a paid trial of the new answer tool and test ten booking changes against real records if errors can be reported openly. In the first year standard calls move, I’d apply for a posted paid complaint role only if its offered wage and hours cover our mortgage, while cutting our monthly paid outing if my hours fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with a way to test the tool. I can learn a new system after seeing it work, but I need paid hours while doing it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the trial measure?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would record whether the tool keeps the customer’s new booking date, not just whether it sounds polite. A missed date sends the person back to our queue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Amir check in an offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Amir (my partner) the offered hours before changing jobs. An hourly rate can look better while the weekly pay is worse.

say: I’d ask the centre for **wrong-answer rates** before it changes our paid hours.
I’d tell colleagues **routine bookings** may move first.
think: I think my **ordinary calls** could shrink despite experience.
I know neither household **wage alone** covers the mortgage.
do: Test **ten booking changes** on paid time with open error reporting in 2026.
Seek **posted complaint work** with offered mortgage-covering wage and hours in the first year.
Cut our **monthly paid outing** only if my call hours fall.
feel: **Anxious** about fewer calls, ready to test a tool.
S1.quote: An hourly rate can look better while the weekly pay is worse.
fieldNote: She tests **new software** on changed booking dates.
She compares **weekly pay**, not only hourly rates.
The household’s **thin reserve** makes paid trials essential.
Her **variable household income** makes an altered roster risky.

steps.text: Test ten booking changes with the new tool on paid time if errors are reportable

Cancel the monthly paid outing if her call hours fall

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could answer calls, make notes and check them too. I would ask the centre for written notice and posted paid roles before the queue changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could remove most of my headset shift in 2028. Robots around 2031 do not delay that; under a month saved would not keep our mortgage current for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for the staffing timetable and stop plans to replace our living-room chairs. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for posted paid service work only if offered hours and wage cover our mortgage, and ask Amir’s brother whether he can collect the children for a booked interview if we cannot both get away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. Less than one month of expenses is not a bridge across a lost headset wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which purchase would you delay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Amir (my partner) the chairs still work. We can keep that money for the mortgage rather than buy comfort now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could someone handle school pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Amir’s brother might be free after his shift, but I would ask only once an interview is confirmed. We cannot count on him as a regular school pickup.

say: I’d ask management for **written notice** and posted paid roles before the call queue changes.
I’d say **2028 thinking AI** reaches headset work first.
think: I think AGI could remove **most calls** in 2028.
I fear a **mortgage gap** with under a month saved.
do: Defer the **chair purchase** and seek staffing dates in 2026.
Apply for **posted paid service work** after 2028 at mortgage-covering offered wage and hours.
Ask Amir’s brother about **school pickup** only if a booked interview prevents both parents from collecting children.
S2.quote: Less than one month of expenses is not a bridge across a lost headset wage.
fieldNote: She sees **thinking AI**, not 2031 robots, as the immediate threat.
The **chairs remain usable**, making delay practical.
Childcare from Amir’s brother is **uncertain** and tied to a booked interview.

steps.text: Delay replacing usable living-room chairs to protect mortgage money
Apply for posted paid service work with offered wage and hours covering mortgage
Ask if Amir’s brother can cover pickup if a booked interview leaves both parents unavailable

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us time to see whether complaint checking is a real paid job. I would ask for posted vacancies with wages before taking a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my years handling calls might help in complaint review, but full AGI could reason through those cases too. I cannot spend our mortgage money on training with no job at the end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take a funded complaint-review course on paid time only if a posted paid role requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that role only if its offered wage and hours cover our mortgage; otherwise I’d keep paid calls while looking at the few nearby centres.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years gives me time to ask hard questions about the role. A course certificate cannot stand in for a mortgage-covering job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask a reviewer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask a current reviewer to show me three complaints that came back after a wrong automated answer. If the posted job actually includes fixing them, the course might be useful.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Amir need to see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Amir (my partner) the vacancy, starting hours and training pay. We can talk about a change after those numbers are written down.

say: I’d ask for **posted complaint jobs** with wages.
I’d say five years gives **time to test** review work.
think: I think my **call experience** could help in review.
I doubt review work has **permanent safety** from AGI.
do: Take a **funded review course** only on paid time for a posted role.
Apply for **posted complaint work** after 2031 only at mortgage-covering wage and hours.
Keep **paid calls** while searching if no mortgage-covering review offer appears.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect the role.
S3.quote: A course certificate cannot stand in for a mortgage-covering job.
fieldNote: She wants **real reopened complaints** in training.
The course requires **funded paid time** and a posted role.
Offered **weekly hours** must preserve the mortgage payment.

steps.text: Take funded complaint-review course on paid time only for a posted paid role
Apply for posted review work with offered wage and hours covering mortgage after 2031
Keep paid calls while searching if no mortgage-covering review offer appears

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to save and learn, if the centre shows which roles stay paid. I would ask for yearly figures on human call hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could move into complaint work by 53, but AGI may still take thinking tasks in that job. Robots around 2039 arrive later; our mortgage comes each month until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls and put a fixed amount from each pay into savings. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid complaint work only if my hours fall and its offered wage and hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about today’s thin cushion, less rushed about 2036. Ten years before AGI reaches my calls in 2036 does not pay the mortgage due next month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which yearly figure matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask how many agent hours were actually paid each year, not just how many calls were handled. A faster system could hide a smaller rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children at their school unless Amir (my partner) and I had a signed offer and a route we can manage. We can search nearby first.

say: I’d ask for **yearly paid call hours** so staff can see a shrinking roster early.
I’d demand **real wages** on any future-role plan.
think: I think I could reach **complaint work** by 53.
I know **2036 thinking AI** could take review tasks too.
do: Keep **taking calls** and save a fixed amount from each pay.
Apply for **posted complaint work** after 2036 if hours fall and pay covers mortgage.
feel: **Anxious** about current bills, less rushed by 2036.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI reaches my calls in 2036 does not pay the mortgage due next month.
fieldNote: Her **thin cushion** keeps present money worry alive.
She asks for **paid agent hours**, not total calls handled.
A move requires a **signed offer** and workable school route.

steps.text: Keep answering calls while the centre pays for shifts
Put a fixed amount from each pay into mortgage savings
Apply for posted complaint work if hours fall and offered wage and hours cover mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. My calls and notes are thinking work, and I cannot keep the mortgage current through a long gap with less than a month saved. I would need notice, a paid trial for a posted role, and offered hours and wages that cover the house.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how a customer knows the note is right. A calm voice cannot fix a wrong account number; I read the number back before ending a call.

headlineQuote: A calm voice cannot fix a wrong account number; I read the number back before ending a call.
portrait: At **43**, Freya is an experienced, average-skill call agent after secondary school and earns lower pay.
She and Amir support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with less than one month saved.
She uses AI **occasionally** once colleagues show its limits.
Few nearby jobs and variable delivery shifts make **paid offers** and notice crucial.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her screen work before the household can afford a long search.
whatWouldHelp: **Notice**, a paid trial and posted mortgage-covering hours and wages would help.
